newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK Grid seen accepting new price plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK Grid seen accepting new price plans.

text.p: Britain's electricity consumers could be in for savings of a billion pounds ($1.6 billion) as the National Grid transmission system looks likely to bow to amended price controls laid out by watchdog OFFER on Thursday.
"My feeling is that it will probably accept" the proposals, said Andrew Stone, analyst at Daiwa Securities.

OFFER's proposals include a one-off reduction in the first year of new controls from April 1, 1997 of 20 percent followed by a cap on price increases of four points below inflation, or RPI-4, for the following three years to 2001.
OFFER head Stephen Littlechild said domestic customers should see average price cuts of four pounds a year from the proposals, adding up to a billion pounds in total.
In a statement, OFFER said National Grid stood to gain or lose up to 21 million pounds in 1997-98 depending on its success in responding to incentives in the proposals.
"It is a tough proposal but a realistic one," he told BBC radio.
The final one-off cut proposed is at the bottom end of a 20-26 percent range outlined by OFFER in August. Those plans also called for curbs on future price changes of RPI-4.
National Grid said those proposals were "contrived, illogical and inconsistent," and said its revenues could be sliced by 200-300 million pounds a year.
This time round, National Grid said it would review the latest proposals and respond to OFFER by October 30.

If it doesn't like the proposals, it could follow British Gas, which turned down price proposals from regulator Ofgas for its own transmission business, TransCo, on Thursday, and opt for an inquiry by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
But analysts felt National Grid was unlikely to seek a referral to the MMC, despite a prolonged war of words with the regulator in the run-up to the final proposals.
"It would cost a lot of time and trouble to go to the MMC. I don't think they are that unhappy," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The stock market appeared to agree that OFFER's proposals brought little novelty, with National Grid shares edging half a penny lower to 178 pence by 1118 GMT.
"The share price reaction should be mildly positive although the upside is limited to five percent," the analyst said.
The latest proposals change the asset valuation basis, one of the main bones of contention, to 4.15 billion pounds, an increase of 150 million pounds from earlier proposals.
OFFER said this reflected a lower attributed value of National Grid's Energis telecommunications business at flotation.
The latest proposals also assume capital expenditure of 775 million pounds, 60 million pounds above earlier assumptions and cuts in controllable operating costs of four percent per year.
"I don't think the cost cutting required is too drastic, despite all the huffing and hawing," said one analyst. ($1=.6388 Pound)
